task_instance: Created a small sample Solidity contract (contracts/VaultSample.sol) with a mix of public, onlyOwner, onlyGuardian, dynamic-trust, callback, and view/pure functions, then manually performed the entry-point analysis workflow (language detection, locate contracts, extract state-changing external functions, classify access level, generate structured markdown report) and produced entry-point-analysis.md in the skill's required output format.
evidence: Wrote contracts/VaultSample.sol (9 state-changing functions: deposit, withdraw, approveSpender, setFee, transferOwnership, pause, unpause, execute, onFlashLoan; plus 2 excluded view/pure functions balanceOf and computeFee). The skill's own workflow explicitly allows falling back to manual analysis using reference files when Slither/tooling is unavailable ('If which slither returns nothing, proceed with manual analysis') and this runtime has no shell to run Slither anyway, so this is not a blocker but the documented fallback path. Manually parsed the file's functions, visibility, and modifiers, classified each into Public/Role-Restricted(Admin,Guardian)/Restricted-Review-Required/Contract-Only per the skill's classification rules, and wrote entry-point-analysis.md following the exact report structure (Summary table with counts, per-category tables with Function/File/Notes or Restriction columns, Files Analyzed section, Analysis Warnings section). Verified the report's counts (3 public + 4 role-restricted + 1 review-required + 1 contract-only = 9) match the 9 state-changing functions in the source file, and confirmed the two view/pure functions were correctly excluded and noted. Deliverable file: entry-point-analysis.md in the work directory. No Bash/shell, no code execution, no MCP/connector tools, and no binary files were used or needed for this deliverable.
